title: Critics warned about Flock surveillance. Three Houston-area investigations are fueling those concerns.

reading.body:
This incident shows a surveillance system being used outside the conditions it was built for. The system was intended for official law enforcement queries, but an authorized user ran repeated searches on the same license plates for personal reasons. The failure was in how the system was used, not in the system's technical performance. The searches continued for years and came to light only after a resident complaint, so catching them earlier would have required a routine audit of search logs against active investigations or a requirement that each query be tied to a case number.

What is not established is whether the searches caused harm or were intended to cause harm. The resident's complaint alleged stalking, but that allegation was not tested in a criminal proceeding. The internal affairs investigation found a policy violation and imposed a suspension, but no criminal charges were filed, and the lieutenant said the information was not used or shared.

reports.title: Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office lieutenant admits to improper use of Flock cameras per docs
Critics warned about Flock surveillance. Three Houston-area investigations are fueling those concerns.

summary:
A Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office lieutenant improperly searched license plate information using Flock cameras on multiple occasions between January 2022 and December 2025. Documents show the lieutenant looked up one license plate 41 times and another 148 times, with the searches unrelated to official law enforcement duties. The lieutenant admitted to the improper use after a resident filed a complaint alleging stalking and expressing fear for their family's safety. The lieutenant claimed concern that the drivers were lurking near their home, and documents indicated there was a contentious family relationship involved.

An internal affairs investigation determined the lieutenant violated department policies and received a two-day suspension. No criminal charges were filed. The lieutenant stated they did not use the retrieved information for any purpose and did not share it with others. A legal expert noted that for such violations to result in criminal consequences rather than administrative discipline, there must be clear intent to cause harm or personal gain. The Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office has not yet responded to requests for further comment on the matter.
